event_model_payload.headline: All Infamy Edicts In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Vampire Court Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Do you want to increase your infamy in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Coen’s Infamy or Notoriety represents how effectively you’ve disrupted the operations of the vampire boyars in Vale Sangora. The more activities you complete, the greater their ire, culminating in epic battles where you can finally put them out of their misery. We're going to tackle all of these mechanics, but be forewarned that there are some spoilers ahead.

In This Article
  • The Blood of Dawnwalker - Vampire Court and Infamy
    • Court activities - Types and completion
    • Infamy effects and Edicts

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Vampire Court and Infamy

You can check your Infamy in The Blood of Dawnwalker via the Court menu. In it, you’ll see the knyaz, Brencis, and his three lieutenants/boyars: Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe.

  • The three boyars have their own respective operations denoted by smaller diamond heraldry connected to their portraits.
  • The smaller pips are missions, which you can click on and track via the Journal. This makes it easier to spot them on the world map.
  • The color of each boss’ portrait also shows if they’re active, angered, or defeated. (Note that clicking on a portrait shows that boyar's "anger meter" of sorts.)
  • The bottom of the panel shows your current Infamy level.

Court activities - Types and completion

The Vampire Court in The Blood of Dawnwalker has their own fiefdoms and responsibilities. Ambrus, whose strongholds are in the northern part of Vale Sangora, handles blood tithes and transportation. Bakir, who controls the southwest, mixes alcohol with blood in distilleries, while also punishing innocent people in pillories. As for Xanthe, she conducts research into the esoteric, as well as abducts young women for her experiments.

The vast majority of these activities cost 3x Time Segments to complete. It’s important to plan ahead in case you want to tackle several of them in quick succession. Likewise, there are activities that won’t be available until you discover clues:

  • Ambrus: Prisoner Processing Camp - Head to the military camp in Stoneward Post and free prisoners. This is done during The Firebrand/Under Watchful Eyes.
  • Bakir: Uriash Village - Ally or destroy the Uriash Village. This is done during Song of the Mountain.
  • Xanthe: Gargoyle Manufacture - Escape the astrologer’s trap and complete Home Sweet Home.

From left to right: Destroying Ambrus' blood supplies, rescuing people from Bakir's pillories, and exorcising demons in Xanthe's excavation sites.

Infamy effects and Edicts

Each activity that you complete increases your Notoriety in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Upon reaching new levels, Brencis will enact a new Edict that’s meant to impede your progress. This happens at the start of each day, where a cutscene shows a herald holding a scroll.

  • Level 1: Additional patrols in settlements.
  • Level 2: Military checkpoints appear throughout the valley.
  • Level 3: Price increases throughout the valley.
  • Level 4: Additional soldiers patrol the roads and commanders now recognize you.
  • Level 5: Fewer people outdoors between dusk and dawn.
  • Level 6: More military checkpoints and further price increases.
  • Level 7: Headhunters appear in the valley and all soldiers now recognize Coen.
  • Level 8: All soldiers become stronger.
  • Level 9: Svartrau City’s gates are shut.

Think of Infamy and Edicts in The Blood of Dawnwalker as akin to your Wanted Level in the Grand Theft Auto series or similar games, except the punishments are permanent. The level 8 Edict makes combat a slog, while the level 9 Edict creates hassles if you’re trying to enter Svartrau City. Your best bet is to climb the walls at night, though you can also look for openings and damaged sections to squeeze through during the day.

As such, we recommend focusing on exploration and doing non-Court-related quests for the first dozen hours or so of the campaign. If you’ve already completed a lot of side content early on, then the added challenge presented by these Edicts won’t be as impactful.

What else happens when you have high Infamy?

There are other things that need to be considered as you raise Infamy or anger vampire lords:

  • At Notorious tier--i.e. Infamy level 4--you’ll fulfill the first step of the Where Loyalty Lies quest. This allows you to finally meet and join the Manumits.
  • Also at Notorious tier, a messenger will give Anca a letter. Pay her a visit in the Crossroads Inn and read the notes. You’ll learn of components that you need to find to make the legendary Arbiter armor set. We discuss this process in detail in our A Bulwark Against Darkness guide.
  • If you keep disrupting the operations of a particular vampire lord, to the point that their anger level is maxed out, you’ll unlock a quest that allows you to finally fight them.
  • Lastly, if you max out your Infamy level, Brencis will actually ask for a parley. He’ll offer you a deal: Your family’s freedom in exchange for betraying the Manumits.

That does it for our guide on how to increase your Infamy in The Blood of Dawnwalker. While we’re on the subject of angering the vrakhiri, you might be curious as to what quests you’d unlock. We tackle these in our article about Ambrus: The Gilded Gauntlet, Bakir: The Lunar Game, and Xanthe: The Cycle of Love.

Lastly, if you're raring to duke it out with these major bosses, we encourage you to read our vrakhiri boss guide and legendary weapons/armors guide.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Defeat All Vampire Court Bosses In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you wondering about how to defeat all major bosses in The Blood of Dawnwalker? These creatures of the night have lorded over the valley, murdering and punishing those they deem unfit to serve them. Now, they’ve also taken Coen’s family, and you must find a way to bring them down. Our guide has all the details that you need, but be forewarned that there will be major spoilers ahead.

In This Article
  • The Blood of Dawnwalker vampire court bosses - Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe
    • How to defeat Ambrus, the Right Fist of the Knyaz
    • How to defeat Bakir, the Mad Khan
    • How to defeat Xanthe, the Dark Mistress
    • How to defeat Brencis, the Knyaz of Vale Sangora

The Blood of Dawnwalker vampire court bosses - Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe

Three of the four major bosses in The Blood of Dawnwalker can be fought as part of general campaign progression. The last one, their leader, Brencis, is pretty much part of the game’s finale. The game basically ends once you beat him.

In the case of Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe, they have their own operations/activities that you can disrupt. We discuss these facets in detail in our Infamy Edicts guide, but here’s a quick summary nonetheless:

  • As you keep sabotaging each boyar’s domain, their anger will rise.
  • At maximum anger level, you receive an important quest that allows you to fight that boss.
  • Once that boss has been defeated, you can kill them outright or drink their blood to obtain a unique vampiric ability. You may also invite their soul into your very being. They’ll just make snide remarks and off-handed quips from time to time.

Note 1: These foes are quite challenging, so we advise you to equip legendary weapons and armors, as well as pick the best skills/perks, before facing them.

Note 2: There's another powerful vampire lord somewhere in Vale Sangora, though you only meet him during a companion's quest. You can learn more about this sequence in our Lacra: Our Rotten Roots guide.

How to defeat Ambrus, the Right Fist of the Knyaz

Ambrus controls the northern part of Vale Sangora, so you’ll probably run into his soldiers early on after the prologue. His quest leads to a one-on-one duel and, during the battle, you have to beware of his martial prowess. He certainly emphasizes finesse over brute strength with his abilities:

  • Cleaving Lunge - Ambrus moves backward then switches to a ready stance, before teleporting and cleaving the area where you’re standing.
  • Eightfold Slice - Similar to the above, Ambrus will prepare to strike, and he’ll do multiple slashes while moving forward.
  • Peerless Bladesman - It’ll be hard to get past Ambrus’ guard, so you have to do a perfect block followed by a riposte to deal damage.
  • Scarlet Shield - Ambrus’ protection also heals him if you attack him while it’s active.
  • Terror in the Shadows - When Ambrus is low on health, he’ll start teleporting continuously while stabbing at your position.

The Ambrus fight in The Blood of Dawnwalker is all about landing strikes with deftness and precision. However, if you do a related quest, you’ll inflict him with a debilitating poison. You just need to dodge his attacks until he’s dead. You can learn more about this method in our The Gilded Gauntlet/The Bittersweet Toast guide.

How to defeat Bakir, the Mad Khan

Bakir was once the leader of a long-forgotten khanate. Now, he just toys with his opponents, goading them into joining deadly contests.

  • Fists of Fury - Bakir is vicious at close range, attacking with a flurry of blows.
  • Flying Kick - Bakir can also teleport and kick Coen in the face.
  • Ground Cascade - Bakir’s favorite move involves slamming the ground and creating a bloody eruption that travels in a straight line.

In Bakir’s boss quest, The Lunar Game, you participate in a battle royale of sorts where you start with low-tier/common gear. All the while, you have to avoid raising his suspicion, which means you can’t use your vampiric abilities.

How to defeat Xanthe, the Dark Mistress

Xanthe is a master of the arcane arts, using her knowledge of sorceries to experiment on women and her own malevolent contraptions. The Xanthe boss fight in The Blood of Dawnwalker takes place in the Howling Keep. It’s part of a quest called The Cycle of Love, where your initial goal is to use lanterns to reach other rooms in the fortress.

Xanthe’s abilities include:

  • Wicked Tendrils - Lashes out with whip-like tentacles/tendrils in succession. You can hold down the block button, then press directional prompts depending on where each tendril is coming from. She’ll get staggered momentarily if you can block several attacks.
  • Boiling Blood - Xanthe causes exploding glyphs to appear on the ground.
  • Life Leech - Xanthe will leech your health to restore her own.
  • Life Orbs - Xanthe has a couple of health thresholds. Upon breaking these thresholds, she’ll spawn several orbs that regenerate her health. You have to destroy these to prevent her from healing back to full.
  • Blood Rush - Once the boss’ HP is down to the last segment, she’ll often rush to your location and then do Boiling Blood at close range.

It’s also worth noting that Xanthe appears in another location: the Svartrau City Cathedral. We’ve seen her there at night and fairly early in the campaign. You can try to defeat her there--i.e. try to use Death From Above to deal tremendous damage at the start.

How to defeat Brencis, the Knyaz of Vale Sangora

The Blood of Dawnwalker’s final boss is Brencis, the leader of the cadre of boyars ruling over Vale Sangora. There are three occasions where you’re able to battle him:

  • Prologue - This is when Coen gets turned into a vrakhir. Brencis is too powerful at this stage, so trying to beat him here is next to impossible.
  • Parley - Upon reaching maximum Infamy, Brencis will invite you to a parlay. There’s an option to fight him, though it’s also possible to team up with him against several spectral foes. In the end, he’ll offer a deal before leaving: He’ll free your family, but you have to betray the Manumit rebels.
  • Finale - This is the conclusion of the campaign and how it happens is entirely up to you. You can either strike out on your own or look for allies that can assist you. You then infiltrate Castle Greifberg, face off against corrupted soldiers and monstrosities, and duke it out against Brencis in the depths of the citadel.

Brencis’ humanoid form isn’t the only one that you need to contend with. After fully depleting his health, he’ll transport you to Anachora, a realm that’s considered the “hell” for the souls of vampires. Brencis reveals his Grotesque Ascendant form, which has the following abilities:

  • Many-Limbed Horror - Several melee attacks where he utilizes his malformed limbs are unblockable.
  • Belching Blood - Brencis will spew forth a torrent of blood from his mouth.
  • Displacement - The screen will flicker, and Brencis will follow up with a teleport to your location.

The aforementioned vampire boyars--Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe--can, surprisingly, help you during this encounter. If you managed to invite them in--i.e. their soul is now part of Coen’s very being--they will manifest in the Anachora portion of the fight. Ambrus will do his Eightfold Slice, Bakir will zip around with his Flying Kick, and Xanthe will strike with Wicked Tendrils.

Once you defeat Brencis, that’s it, the game is over. You don’t continue exploring the rest of Vale Sangora and there’s no New Game Plus mode to look forward to. All that’s left is to experience the conclusion of Coen’s journey…at least for now.

That does it for our guide on how to defeat the Vampire Court bosses in The Blood of Dawnwalker. How you advance through to the finale is entirely up to you. That said, you might want to know about all the endings in the game, including secret outcomes.

event_model_payload.headline: Should You Invite Vampire Lords In The Blood Of Dawnwalker?
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you deciding on whether or not you should invite vampire lords in The Blood of Dawnwalker? The vrakhiri--Brencis, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe--have ravaged the entirety of Vale Sangora. They’ve killed thousands of people and ruined the lives of countless others. They’ve turned entire settlements into charnel houses and they’ve feasted on the anguished cries of the innocent.

But, hey, maybe inviting their soul still seems like a good idea. Let's discuss if this particular facet is worth the trouble, and be ready for spoilers, too.

In This Article
  • The Blood of Dawnwalker - Inviting a vrakhiri’s soul while in Anachora
    • No downsides to inviting a vampire
    • The final battle in Anachora

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Inviting a vrakhiri’s soul while in Anachora

The act of inviting a vampire in The Blood of Dawnwalker, surprisingly enough, doesn’t offer any downsides. Here’s how it occurs:

  • First, you need to increase your Infamy level by sabotaging the operations of the vampire boyars. Once a vampire lord has been angered enough, you’ll receive a quest where you’ll be able to eliminate them for good.
  • When you fight and defeat a vampire lord--and assuming it’s nighttime/Coen is in vampire form--you’ll be presented an option to drink their blood.
  • If you drink their blood, you’ll obtain their unique skill.
  • This action also transports you to Anachora, also known as the hell for every damned vampiric soul.

No downsides to inviting a vampire

While you’re in Anachora, you’ll have a chat with the soul of the vampire boyar that you just defeated. Some might beg you to show mercy, while others are just happy staying in that nightmarish realm.

Through dialogue options, you can just tell your foe that you’re “inviting them in” (or any statement of a similar effect). This causes their soul/essence to meld with Coen’s consciousness.

For the most part, their disembodied voices will just make snide remarks or warn you of dangers. It’s like having someone going “tsk tsk” every now and then. It’s not really as annoying at first glance.

Note: The vampire boyars aren't the only ones whose souls can be tied to yours. You might even meet an ancient lord while undertaking a female companion's quest chain.

The final battle in Anachora

The vampire boyars that you invite do contribute near the end of the campaign when you finally face Brencis. The second phase of the battle transitions to Anachora, where Brencis will transform into the Grotesque Ascendant.

If you already have the souls of Ambrus, Bakir, and/or Xanthe, they’ll periodically attack Brencis. You’ll see Bakir’s flying kicks, Ambrus’ twirling slashes, and Xanthe’s bloody whips, all hitting Brencis when the opportunity arises.

So, yes, inviting a vampire in The Blood of Dawnwalker is really a good idea. But, before you could do that, you might want to know how to defeat all of these bosses in the first place.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Romance Crake In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you wishing you could romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This formidable warrior also happens to be the leader of the Manumits, a group of rebels seeking to overthrow the vrakhiri in Vale Sangora. What starts out as mere camaraderie between Coen and Crake might develop into something deeper.

In This Article
  • The Blood of Dawnwalker - Crake romance guide
    • What Hunts the Night
    • What Moves the Dead
    • Distant Shadows
    • A Closer Look: Crake sex/romance scene

The Blood of Dawnwalker - Crake romance guide

It’s going to take a bit of effort before you can romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker. That’s because you have to join the Manumits first. Here’s a quick summary:

  • Straight out of the prologue, you could try to complete The Firebrand quest.
  • This leads to another mission called Shadows in the Woods, which is where you’ll meet the Manumits: Crake, Drogos, and Sara.
  • The Manumits don’t trust Coen yet, so you have to prove yourself to them by increasing your Infamy level. Once you reach level 4 (Notorious), the quest step for Where Loyalty Lies will change. You’ll be able to enter the Manumits hideout and proceed with the next steps.

What Hunts the Night

You’ll have an opportunity to learn more about Crake during What Hunts the Night. When Coen and Crake decide to hide in a building, there are dialogue options where you can have Crake open up more.

  • “Do you want to talk about Sara?”
  • “You sure? You look upset.”
  • “I know what it’s like to lose someone.” - If you’ve already completed Home Sweet Home, then you can talk a bit about Coen’s past trauma.
  • “Maybe we could talk about them instead.”
  • “Alin loved apples.”

What Moves the Dead

The next part of the Crake romance in The Blood of Dawnwalker takes place in What Moves the Dead. After Coen and Crake escape from the crypts, you’ll have the option to “walk him back to the hideout.” This costs 1x Time Segment, but you’ll also learn that Crake’s real name is Marat.

Inside the hideout, you’ll have a chance to bandage Crake’s/Marat’s wounds:

  • “Let me help.”
  • “Not that bad.”
  • “Sure.”

Distant Shadows

This portion of Crake’s story arc might seem like a throwaway quest, but you need to tackle it if you want to romance him. Your goal is to follow a man named Ascar:

  • While trailing Ascar, hide behind obstacles so you don’t get spotted.
  • There are soldiers in the village. Stay several feet away from them. If they recognize Coen, it’s all over.
  • Follow Ascar through the woods and, near the end, you’ll see him accosted by the soldiers. You can save him if you’d like or just stay hidden.
  • If Ascar spotted you, you can ask him if he knows of a person named Marat.

Back at the hideout, talk to Crake and tell him what happened. Be honest. He’ll storm off, but his lieutenant, Drogos, will tell you where he went. Say that you’ll go talk to him.

A Closer Look: Crake sex/romance scene

And this is the part where you get to romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Keep in mind that A Closer Look is a time-sensitive quest. You must complete it within the same cycle--i.e. If it’s nighttime, then you can’t advance to the next day.

In any case, go to the marked location and have a chat with Crake. Pick the following options:

  • “May I join you then?”
  • “I’m worried about you. What’s wrong?’
  • “Please, just tell the truth about Ascar.”
  • “Hey, nothing you say can change the way I see you.”

You’ll learn that Ascar is Crake’s father, and he left on bad terms after his dad found out about his sexuality. At this stage, Crake will kiss Coen, only for the latter to get startled. Now, you just need to pick this option: [Kiss him back].

After the scene, you can continue chatting with Crake. Coen can also share that his mother might’ve been aware that he’s bisexual, causing the two warriors to come to an understanding. From here, Crake tells you about his plan to defeat Brencis, which eventually leads to his own finale quest.

That does it for our guide on how to romance Crake in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you want Coen to find more partners, you can read our Anca romance guide and Lacra romance guide.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Complete A Deal With The Devil In The Blood Of Dawnwalker
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you hoping to complete A Deal with the Devil in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This is one of the most important quests in the game, though it’s going to take several hours before you even have access to it. Once you tackle it, though, you’ll be presented with crucial decisions that can shape the fates of characters. Our guide has all the info you need, but be ready for spoilers as well.

In This Article
  • A Deal with the Devil - Unlock requirement
    • A parlay with Brencis
    • The crucial choice
    • What happens if you fight Brencis?
    • What happens if you betray the Manumits?

A Deal with the Devil - Unlock requirement

A Deal with the Devil in The Blood of Dawnwalker only becomes available once you reach the maximum Infamy level. This means you must do various vampire court activities, such as sabotaging distilleries, ambushing blood transports, freeing kidnapped prisoners, and more. Likewise, you’ll want to eliminate some or all of Brencis’ vampire lieutenants, too.

Upon reaching maximum Infamy, wait until the next day until you get the herald cutscene. You’ll then receive a letter saying that Brencis has invited you to a parlay.

A parlay with Brencis

Once the quest appears in your journal, simply travel to the marked location: Shrike’s Crag. Ensure that it’s nighttime and climb up the Scouting Tower. Near the top, you’ll see a brazier that you can light. This action costs 4x Time Segments. Be sure to make a backup save at this stage.

Upon lightning the signal fire, a short cutscene will play. Brencis will arrive with Coen’s father, Pieter, in tow. You have the option to talk to Pieter first--you can also hug him to prove that you’re real and still alive (albeit turned into a vampire).

Brencis will then tell you a little bit about history and of how Shrike’s Crag was the site of a massacre. The previous knyaz, Skender, once killed every peasant who had surrendered to him. He then says that he intends to continue ruling, and that a brewing rebellion fomented by the Manumits must stop.

The crucial choice

In The Blood of Dawnwalker Deal with a Devil quest, you’re given multiple choices on how to respond:

  • “I just want my family back” and “What do I have to do with it?” - These options lead to Brencis offering you a deal. He’ll free your family, but you have to betray the Manumits. You can then say that “I’ll do it” or “I’ll think about it.”
  • During the conversation, you’ll also notice at least one option with a sword icon. This will trigger a boss battle against Brencis.

Note 1: Even if you’re considering the deal, you don’t have to go through with betraying the Manumits. You can still tackle other quests and progress through the finale via other means.

Note 2: If you choose any option that doesn't lead to combat, dozens of Vidmo Specters and Spectral Skeletons will appear all around Shrike's Crag. Don't worry because Brencis will be fighting alongside you at this stage. After the encounters, Brencis will take Pieter with him as he teleports back to Greifberg Castle.

What happens if you fight Brencis?

Let’s say you actually engage Brencis in combat:

  • You fight Brencis’ humanoid form during the first phase, though you also have to deal with dozens of Vidmo Specter enemies.
  • Then, upon depleting Brencis’ health, you have to eliminate him while in the hellish realm of Anachora.

Unfortunately, even if you’re victorious here, you won’t be able to celebrate. A cutscene will play showing that Coen’s father was killed while you were fighting Brencis. During and after the epilogue at Laslea Glen, you’ll realize that the rest of Coen’s family is gone, too.

And it really makes sense when you think about it. Brencis’ forces have been holding Coen’s family hostage the entire time. Coen was invited to a parlay, where hostilities weren’t allowed. Coen then attacked and killed Brencis.

The fact that Coen’s Infamy had greatly risen in less than a month--i.e. you’ve killed too many vampire-aligned soldiers--would make the average person think that he’s a bloodthirsty maniac. Killing a lord who has your loved ones, as expected, would lead to the execution of said loved ones.

What happens if you betray the Manumits?

Okay, so what can you expect if you betray the Manumits in The Blood of Dawnwalker? First, make sure you’ve already completed the Where Loyalty Lies quest so that you’re invited to the Manumit hideout. Then, walk up to the entrance door of the building and mark it with Brencis’ blood.

This leads to a cutscene where Brencis flies through the windows, tossing out a few rebels. He then stabs Crake’s throat with his claws, before thanking Coen with a nod. You then get to experience the epilogue back at Laslea Glen.

That does it for our guide on how to complete A Deal with the Devil in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Again, you don’t need to go through with either of these actions, as you can still change your mind and take the fight to Brencis in his citadel. If you’re curious about how certain events would play out, you can read our spoiler-filled endings and epilogues guide.

event_model_payload.headline: Fall’s Video Game Release Slate Is Intimidatingly Good And Completely Doomed
event_model_payload.summary:
You know it, I know it, and everyone else knows it. The glut of games coming in Fall 2026 is intimidatingly good. But is that overwhelming wave of exciting titles actually hiding a more gruesome reality? I sure think so.

Gaming audiences are no strangers to the rush of fall releases. Even during a slow year, there's almost always an uptick in blockbuster games that launch during this window to best capitalize on the end of the summer and the move toward the winter holidays. This fall is absolutely stuffed with exciting new games around every corner, but it feels more likely for the season to be a bloodbath than a celebration. 

In September alone, I suspect all manner of players will feel a bit spoiled. Early in the month, the co-op '80s anime adventure Orbitals will release exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. On the same day, a very different kind of player will likely dig into The Blood of Dawnwalker, an ambitious vampire RPG with its sights set on dethroning The Witcher series and made by some of its veteran staff. That's some stiff competition just within the first three days of the month.

Capcom will launch its return to Onimusha a day later, and yet another asymmetrical multiplayer game--this time starring Michael Myers and centering on the Halloween series--follows soon after. Valheim, an indie survival game that took the world by storm in early access, will drop its big 1.0 update on September 9. A week later, Runescape Dragonwilds--a pretty similar game in all but name--has its big 1.0 release. Uh-oh. 

I haven't even gotten to the biggest games of the month. PlayStation will finally release Insomniac's long-awaited Wolverine game about halfway through September, only to be one-upped by what is arguably the largest Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive yet with Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. In the midst of that, fans of the Legend of Heroes RPGs get the remake of Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, and at the very end of the month, a one-two punch of Control Resonant and Silent Hill Townfall will pound lovers of all things scary and deeply weird.

There are more games of all sorts to come in October, like a new Ace Combat, a Gears of War prequel, a Hellraiser title, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Modern Warfare 4--not to be confused with Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare--a port of a mobile Final Fantasy, Phantom Blade Zero, and even a collection of Kingdom Hearts games. Hell, we don't have confirmed release dates, but even The Duskbloods and the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time are still supposedly due by the end of the year. 

Of course, all of these games with actual dates are launching ahead of the biggest title of the year, and maybe even all time: Grand Theft Auto 6, which looks like it'll dominate November, the holidays after, and perhaps the entirety of the next few years. 

Much as I want to view this lineup optimistically, it’s hard to see this run of releases as anything but carnage. The games industry has never been more fraught, and now it's about to tear itself apart in a matter of months. Whether a game is good or bad, a hit or a flop, developers and studios are seeing layoffs and even being completely shut down, as parent corporations tighten their belts and watch their stock tickers. All these games are about to go head-to-head vying for a limited number of gamer dollars and eyeballs, which is likely to make all the existing problems in the industry even worse.

Take, as one example, the fact that Riot Games gave its fighting game 2XKO about nine months before winding down its development. If the support of the publisher behind massive ongoing hits such as League of Legends and Valorant can’t provide a modicum of protection for developers, what is saving any of the studios dropping into this fall's free-for-all? And how are we, as consumers, supposed to reasonably prop up all of that?

Now, especially at a time when consumer dollars are being stretched or spent elsewhere, it feels impossible that all of these teams can possibly succeed to the degree they need to in order to survive--or even simply come out of the season unscathed. No matter who wins this fall, it feels like we’ll all lose as a consequence. 

Console spending is down due to a worsening global economy and increased corporate spending on AI, which has brought the cost of systems and some games to an all-time high. Anecdotally, most savvy gamers I know--the types to pick up all kinds of games for a breadth of experiences--are budgeting their time and money carefully for the next few months with so many games dropping on top of one another. Even subscriptions such as Xbox Game Pass, which should be a bounty to budget-conscious consumers, are failing to gain any momentum, and in fact seem to be losing their footholds as discourse over ownership and physical media has intensified. 

Some of these games are simply going to slip through the cracks, and as a result, the whole space will hurt. Sales forecasts will adjust to account for the most contentious season in years. Some games might perform well or even better than expected. I expect countless more will underperform, though. Publishers and developers will downsize teams as a result, despite the likelihood those teams have put out incredible work. And while massive publishers like Capcom, Square Enix, and Nintendo will be mostly protected from absolute devastation, I suspect smaller developers and publishers--like Remedy, which often skirts the line between AA and AAA--will bear a heavy burden should they come up short at the literal worst of times. And that’s to say nothing of independent studios--teams made up of handfuls of hopefuls trying to make a dent at the same time that Rockstar happens to drop what will likely be one of the most successful entertainment launches of all time.

Unfortunately, there seems to be no great solution. Many studios are hemorrhaging as they try to weather this storm the games industry finds itself caught in. Teams can’t simply hold back releases for more opportune release windows, for fear of going under before they can even get their games out the door. Whatever protections may have once existed--lofty publishing deals with Epic Games or contracts to launch titles day one on Game Pass--seem all but gone. It’s everyone for themselves right now, and I fear it's going to bear out in an ugly way come the end of this year.

I'd love to be proven wrong. I want everyone to win. But the reality of the situation seems to be that few will. And if the worst does come to pass and the season takes its toll on these talented developers, as it seems has become common, then this bounty of releases will turn into a bloodbath quickly, and all that'll remain at its end is an increasingly broken games industry without a path forward.

I’ve written about Fanatical’s limited-time mystery bundles a fair amount. I’ve never won any of the major prizes, but I have been fortunate enough to get plenty of new and interesting games in my library. Of course, there are plenty that I haven’t played yet—my backlog is already full enough as it is—but having no shortage of games to choose from is my vibe, and the mystery bundles? I also got Dead Rising 3 Apocalypse Edition, and considering I hadn’t finished the launch version (fans of the Day One box art, unite), I’m happy to finally give it another try. Another one I’m hoping to play soon is Hauntsville, an indie horror survival game with a western twist.

Some lucky buyers could get instant grand prizes, including $1,000's worth of games through the Golden Crates or keys to games like Crimson Desert and Doom: The Dark Ages. Unsurprisingly, these are elusive wins, but they do happen, and it could happen to you. That would certainly be worth bragging about.

Instead of paying $1 / £1 each, you can get 25 keys for $17.49 / £17.49, making them considerably cheaper. Once again, you’re not just spending money for a chance at the hardware—you’re actually getting a game with each crate. The result is random, but the excitement? Priceless. You can buy some Mystery Crates here.

So, don’t waste the opportunity while this bundle is around. Stock up on some indie games, add a few Steam trading cards to your inventory, and cross your fingers for the Steam Machine. You know what? I’ll cross my fingers, too, hoping you get it, dear reader.

event_model_payload.headline: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
event_model_payload.summary:
Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series. 

While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.

The original movie pitch

People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture." 

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.

That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success). 

This was a year after The Last of Us came out in 2013. It was a hot property, as the game was a critical and a commercial success for Naughty Dog and Sony. With Sony also owning and operating its own film studio, all the synergies were there for Sony to make a Last of Us film.

Neil Druckmann, who directed The Last of Us game, confirmed in 2014 that the movie would adapt the story of The Last of Us, as opposed to branching off in some other way. At the time, Druckmann said the movie would "take into account the unique properties of film," but he stressed it was early days and the team hadn't yet mapped out how it would condense the game's story into a two-hour film. In 2015, Druckmann confirmed he had written a second draft of the movie's script, which he said contained "pretty big changes" from the source material.

It was also at this time that Druckmann said a table read had already taken place with "a bunch of actors," though he did not name any outright. Game of Thrones star Maisie Williams was said to be a frontrunner to play Ellie, and many people said that casting was perfect. Williams herself confirmed she met with Druckmann and Raimi about it, but remarked at the time that there was no script or director at that point. Williams, who was 17 at the time, also joked at the time that she hoped Sony would make the movie quickly because, "If they make it in 30 years, they can't have a 40-year-old Ellie." Kaitlyn Dever was also considered for the role of Ellie in the film, and, spoiler alert: Dever would go on to play Ellie's adversary, Abby, in the HBO TV show.

Development Hell

Hollywood productions can take a lot of time to come together, and when the production process goes on for an extended period of time, that's known as "Development Hell." The Last of Us movie was yet another example of this unfortunate phenomenon.

In 2016, Druckmann said the movie hadn't progressed for "over a year" at that point. "It kind of entered development hell like these things tend to do," he said. The movie also never had a director signed on, nor was there a cast or a release date.

This wouldn't be the last time a Naughty Dog film project was subject to development hell, as the Uncharted movie is a very infamous example of this, but that did eventually come together for release in 2022 after a decade of development.

The Last of Us "would have been awful" as a movie

Druckmann said in an interview with Sacred Symbols that movie executives told him to "make it bigger, make it more like World War Z," and he pushed back against this. "Go make World War Z. Why make The Last of Us? The Last of Us is not that," he said. Conversely, Druckmann said HBO boss Casey Bloys told him, "'Do as much action as you need to, and no more. Do as much violence as you need to, and no more. Here, we sell drama.'" 

Druckmann said he got the opposite notes when The Last of Us was envisioned as a feature film. It's not a stretch to imagine this is part of the reason why Naughty Dog opted for a TV show instead of a film, in addition to there being a more supportive and understanding team at HBO to produce and back the show.

Druckmann also said HBO approached the source material with "such reverence and artistry," ensuring Naughty Dog would be involved in the process too. This is not always the case, of course, as the Baldur's Gate TV series at HBO does not involve Larian Studios. Druckmann also mentioned that HBO was supportive of the many changes to the source material that Druckmann and writer/showrunner Craig Mazin made. 

Appearing on Logically Speaking in 2024, Druckmann said the movie version of The Last of Us "would have been awful." He said, "It would have been one of those bad adaptations had we finished that one." 

"You have two hours, max, and the feedback I got was, 'This will lead it down a bad path,'" he added.

In a recent interview with GamesBeat, Druckmann said he changed his mind about how to approach such projects. Whereas in 2014 he said The Last of Us movie would be an adaptation of the game, in 2016, he said Naughty Dog had "evolved our feelings" about adaptations. 

"As time goes on, we are not excited by a direct adaptation of a story for a game into a movie,” Druckmann said. “We have told that story well, cinematically. The idea for The Last of Us film was to be a direct adaptation. I don’t want that movie to be made."

Druckmann indeed got his wish, and that movie was never made. The TV series with HBO, meanwhile, premiered in January 2023, and its first season--starring Bella Ramsey as Ellie and Pedro Pascal as Joel--was a huge success in terms of critical reception and viewership numbers. A second season aired in 2025, and was similarly successful, though not quite to the same degree. A third--and potentially final--season is in the works now, but Druckmann dropped out to focus on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet and other projects at Naughty Dog (maybe The Last of Us 3?).

event_model_payload.headline: How To Complete The Cycle Of Love In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Xanthe Boss Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you befuddled by the tasks in The Cycle of Love in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This quest, which is the conclusion of your battles against Xanthe, takes place in a keep. Along the way, you have to illuminate your surroundings to access new pathways. Oh, and you also have to consider Xanthe’s offer at the end. Our guide has all the info that you need, but be ready for some minor spoilers, too.

In This Article
  • Xanthe’s demise - The Cycle of Love
    • Howling Keep puzzle - Xanthe’s Lanterns
    • Iasmina and the Painted Door
    • Legendaries and manuals
    • The yard and the kennels
    • The Painted Door: Chariklea and Xanthe boss fight
    • The Cycle of Love: Xanthe’s deal and Chariklea’s fate

Xanthe’s demise - The Cycle of Love

The Blood of Dawnwalker Cycle of Love quest appears in your journal once you’ve maxed out Xanthe’s anger toward you. As such, you have to spend some time in the campaign taking out her blood guards and disrupting her research into ancient ruins.

Down the line, one of Brencis’ soldiers, Leonard, will show up and ask you to eliminate Xanthe. He’ll give you a lantern that grants access to her lair, a foreboding castle called Howling Keep. Be ready because you’re about to venture into one of the creepiest areas in the game.

Note 1: Howling Keep is west of Tantari Woods. Once the quest is active, track the “Get to the mansion” objective to make the marker appear on your map.

Note 2: Xanthe also appears in the Svartrau City cathedral at night, and only once fairly early in the game. With a bit of luck and skill, you might just be able to finish her off there.

Howling Keep puzzle - Xanthe’s Lanterns

The key mechanic in The Blood of Dawnwalker Howling Keep puzzle involves Xanthe’s Lanterns. The fortress itself has numerous statues of desiccated humanoids, and placing a lantern in their hand removes the corrupted growths that block your path.

Once you’re inside the main hall, take a look at your surroundings. There’s one statue on the ground floor and two on top of the stairs.

Iasmina and the Painted Door

Let’s start off by heading up the staircase at the back of the main hall:

  • Open the door to the second-floor hallway. You’ll see a statue with a lantern but you don’t need to grab it yet.
  • Enter the room to your right to meet a woman named Iasmina. It seems that she’s terrified of the Painted Door.
  • This painted door is at the end of the hallway, but the path is barred since there are two statues and you need two lanterns.
  • In any case, take the lantern in Iasmina’s room and go back to the staircase overlooking the main hall. Place the lantern in the statue there to prevent the door from being barred.
  • Return to the second-floor hallway outside Iasmina’s room and take the lantern. Then head back to the staircase and grab the lantern that you just placed.

Legendaries and manuals

All right, now you have a couple of lanterns. Here’s what you need to do next in The Blood of Dawnwalker Cycle of Love quest:

  • As you’re walking down the staircase, enter the room to your right and place a lantern in the statue’s hand.
  • In the adjacent room, you’ll find a Cycle of Ruin Manual and a letter from a certain “L.” Looks like there’s another vrakhiri in Svartrau City, and you can meet her in a quest called A Friend Like This. Pick up the lantern when you leave the room.
  • Next, go to the staircase at the opposite side of the main hall. Place the lantern here.
  • The two rooms off to the side should become accessible. You’ll find the Recipe for Venom Claws Ampoule (epic consumable) and Recipe for Potent Aetheric Attunement (legendary consumable).
  • The Relic of St. Dassius is also on a bench. It’s a legendary amulet with witchcraft ability damage, witchcraft health cost, AC restoration (actions), and AC restoration (passive).

The yard and the kennels

After our little looting detour, it’s time to proceed deeper into the keep:

  • Make sure you still have both lanterns with you. Place one of them in the hand of the statue on the ground floor.
  • Enter the yard and defeat the spectral enemies. Then, check the small building just beyond. You’ll find a Recipe for Supernatural’s Blood Infusion (epic consumable) next to the cadaver of a woman.
  • Take the lantern from the statue in this room. This will cause the corrupted growths to disappear, revealing a trapdoor.
  • Drop down and defeat more zombie-like enemies and loot the Key to the Kennels. It unlocks the door that leads you back to the main hall.
  • Take the lantern from the statue on the ground floor and eliminate all the hostiles that spawn.

The Painted Door: Chariklea and Xanthe boss fight

You’ve got three lanterns with you now, so it’s time to conclude The Cycle of Love quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker:

  • Return to the second-floor hallway and go to the end. You’ll be able to place lanterns in the hands of both statues.
  • Pass through the Painted Door and talk to the mysterious girl named Chariklea. (It’s eventually revealed that she’s Xanthe’s daughter.)
  • Suddenly, Xanthe will attack Coen, tossing him back to the yard.

The Xanthe boss fight in The Blood of Dawnwalker can be somewhat tricky due to her mastery of witchcraft and demonic spells:

  • Wicked Tendrils - Lashes out with tendrils/tentacles.
  • Boiling Blood - Creates glyphs on the ground that explode after a short delay.
  • Life Leech - Seeps your health to restore her own.
  • Life Orbs - After depleting each health segment, she’ll spawn several orbs that gradually restore her health.
  • Blood Rush - When she’s low HP, she’ll keep rushing toward you before triggering an explosion.

Xanthe’s Boiling Blood and Blood Rush abilities can be dodged, so no worries there. As for her Wicked Tendrils, you can hold down the block button and press the directional input where each tentacle is coming from. If you can block these in quick succession, she’ll be staggered briefly. As for her Life Orbs, just destroy them quickly to prevent her from regenerating too much health.

Attempting to talk to Chariklea (left) leads to a fight against Xanthe (right).

The Cycle of Love: Xanthe’s deal and Chariklea’s fate

Unlike Ambrus and Bakir, Xanthe doesn’t actually want to die. In fact, she’ll make a deal:

  • If you spare her life, she’ll help you during the finale when you storm Greifberg Castle.
  • Of course, you could still drain her blood. Then, when you end up in Anachora, you can invite her soul or leave her to rot in vrakhiri limbo.

In any case, once you defeat Xanthe in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you’ll receive the following rewards:

  • Blood Surge (only if you drank Xanthe’s blood) - This ability causes your target to explode, but it costs 3x Activation Charges (AC).
  • Corrupted Pendant (legendary amulet) - It has maximum vampiric health, vampiric health segment regeneration, vampiric ability cooldown, and damage against mortals.
  • Potent Aetheric Attunement (legendary consumable) - Grants +15% witchcraft ability damage.

Lastly, as for Chariklea, you have the option to end her suffering or spare her life. The choice is entirely up to you.

That does it for our guide on how to complete The Cycle of Love in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you’re curious about a court activity related to Xanthe, you can check our Home Sweet Home guide. We also have guides for the other major bosses, namely Ambrus: The Gilded Gauntlet and Bakir: The Lunar Game.

event_model_payload.summary:
Are you intrigued by the existence of Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker? These beings, a cross between a moth and a pixie, are fairies who live in small burrows underground. Don’t let their diminutive size fool you, because they’re quite tricky and mischievous, too. However, if you can help them out, you might just receive the most important resource in the game: Time.

Our guide has all the information that you need. We discuss the Good Home quest and Letters to Lunka quest.

In This Article

    • Good Home: Heile, Tonis, and the ruins of Oghasti
    • Good Home: The Sanzhana Tsarina and communicating with Coen’s sister
    • Letters to Lunka: Pearly and Precious
    • Letters to Lunka: Burrow Sorrows
    • Letters to Lunka: Tiny Dancer
    • Letters to Lunka: Come Hither
    • Sanzhani Fairies reward

All Sanzhani Fairy locations - Good Home and Letters to Lunka guide

There are a total of five Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Here’s the kicker: You won’t be able to see any of them from the get-go. Instead, you have to complete a prerequisite quest called Good Home. From there, you’ll be able to search for the remaining four fairies.

Good Home: Heile, Tonis, and the ruins of Oghasti

First, you have to tackle The Blood of Dawnwalker Good Home quest. Make your way to the quest marker in Svartrau Outskirts and look for a flowerbed with glowing moths.

Follow the glowing insects to the next flowerbed and continue onward until you see a small opening. Crawl through the opening to arrive at a small underground hovel called the Yawning Burrow. There, you’ll meet a little girl named Heile.

  • Heile says that she’s from Oghasti, an abandoned village to the south. Make your way there and investigate her old home. Checking out the axe that’s embedded on the wall costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Next, go to the larger house, which Heile calls the Wooden Palace. When you investigate the second floor, you’ll consume 2x Time Segments.
  • Your next goal is to head to the Coal Burners’ Camp. But, before you do that, bear in mind that there’s another notable quest in Oghasti. It’s called Hedgehog Herb and it grants you an item that increases your maximum health permanently. You can learn more about it in our Hedgehog Herb guide.
  • Anyway, travel to the camp and look for trees marked with an “X.” Watch out for wild animals like bears, and keep your eyes peeled for a lone man who’s sitting by a campfire.
  • Talk to him and give him an alcoholic drink. Don’t offer to help him with his task as that costs 3x Time Segments.
  • You’ll learn that the man is named Tonis, and he’s actually Heile’s older brother. At this stage, you can have Tonis accompany you straight back to the Yawning Burrow.

Meet up with Heile (left) and investigate Oghasti (middle). Eventually, you'll meet Heile's brother, Tonis (right).

Good Home: The Sanzhana Tsarina and communicating with Coen’s sister

You’ll then have an encounter with your first Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker. It’s none other than the Sanzhani Tsarina. Try to convince Tonis that Heile’s better off in the burrow to proceed with the next part of the quest chain.

At this point, the Sanzhani Tsarina will tell you that her kind can help you communicate with your sister Lunka. This begins the Letters to Lunka quest. Here’s what you need to know about it:

  • You can ask the Sanzhani to deliver one message at a time. You’ll receive Lunka’s reply one day-night transition later.
  • Normally, you have to wait for the reply before you can check out the other Sanzhani-related quests. However, we’ve already shown you all the locations in the map above. You can simply go to those areas whenever you want.
  • Each Sanzhani quest that you complete lets you send another message to Lunka. You can just keep returning to the Yawning Burrow whenever you want to ask your sister a new question.

Note: Each Sanzhana quest has actions that cost around 2x Time Segments to complete.

Letters to Lunka: Pearly and Precious

This Letters to Lunka quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker is fairly important. It takes place just south of Stoneward Post--i.e. where you freed Mert during the events of The Firebrand. Investigate the destroyed cart and look for the Sanzhana fairy. Then, follow the trail and kill the bandits.

This particular fairy will turn into a special vendor NPC:

  • She doesn’t want to buy anything from you, save for Shiny Tooth items. She’ll pay you 150 denarii for each.
  • She sells various items, including skill manuals. These still cost denarii.
  • One notable item that she has is the Fear of the Wilds legendary amulet. It has weapon damage, attack stamina cost, damage against animals, and AC restoration (attacks).
  • She also sells a Silk Thread, which is required for a quest called A Bulwark Against Darkness. However, this item costs around 5,750 denarii.
  • Once you leave this location, she’ll move to the Yawning Burrow and she’ll permanently reside there.

This Sanzhana pixie (left) becomes a vendor once you've taken care of the bandits (right).

Letters to Lunka: Burrow Sorrows

This particular quest is fairly straightforward. Go to the location and talk to the Sanzhana. Then, kill the kobolds in the burrow so you can pick up the charm.

Letters to Lunka: Tiny Dancer

This poor Sanzhana in The Blood of Dawnwalker has been imprisoned in a cage. The house that you’re looking for is near the central area of Svartrau City. Activate Focus Mode so you can see the gold-and-green glow emanating from the interior.

You can enter via the second-floor balcony. If it’s nighttime, just use your Shadowstep/Planeshift. If it’s daytime, head up the sloping pathway and do a running jump to cross the gap.

Anyway, once you’re inside the house, grab the Cage Key and free the pixie. She’ll also tell you that the wicked man that trapped her has some silver hidden in the floorboards. It’s up to you if you want to take out the fella to get extra loot.

Letters to Lunka: Come Hither

This is another notable Letters to Lunka quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. The point-of-interest is east of the Silty Mug Inn and north of the Vedera Marsh Guardpost. Chat with the fairy and drop down the cavernous area.

Down below, you have to fight a Murohn, a part-vrakhiri creature that’s ferociously feral. Once you’ve finished off the creature, don’t forget to grab the Silk Threads off to the side. Unlike the item being sold by the Sanzhana from earlier, this one’s completely free.

Sanzhani Fairies reward

That’s it! You’ve helped out all the Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Go ahead and return to the Yawning Burrow and talk to the Sanzhani Tsarina. For your efforts, you’ll receive the most important reward of all: Time.

The Sanzhani have mysterious powers that most humans can’t even fathom, allowing them to play around with time. Since you’ve helped them immensely, you’ll be given +1 extra day--eight segments for daytime and eight segments for nighttime--effectively extending the deadline to save your family.

That does it for our guide on how to help all the Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you’re curious about other magical mysteries in the game, you can head over to our Home Sweet Home/Ambrosius Tower guide.

event_model_payload.headline: NBA 2K’s Best Mode Is Even Better This Year
event_model_payload.summary:
NBA 2K has long been the standard-bearer for high-quality sports games. It's the pinnacle that other series like Madden, FC, and even the oft-beloved MLB The Show aspire to emulate in whatever ways their respective sports allow. That's not to say it gets everything right, but it often feels like the team at Visual Concepts is competing against itself. It creates trends; it doesn't chase them.

That's always been most obvious in The City, the series' social PvPvE hub and the lifeblood of the game's community. Though some other parts of the game are more uneven with this year's entry, The City proves that if you only plan to play one sports game this year, NBA 2K27 is the way to go.

The City is where players can meet up for basketball games of varying sweat levels, buy cosmetics, and complete live-service challenges--it is the center of NBA 2K27's solar system. This hub is thoughtfully attached to the single-player MyCareer mode at the proverbial hip, and this pairing offers more enjoyable and immersive things to do as a tandem than most other sports games taken in their totality. 

This year, The City makes several smart changes. At the core of it all is the long-awaited ability to import custom women characters into the mode. Aesthetically, this is a nice change that lets the hub world better reflect real-life streetball communities--it's always been true that women have existed in these spaces in real life, so they should be included in NBA 2K, too. 

However, this positive change does come with a frustrating caveat: The MyCareer mode doesn't account for them, thereby siloing these women avatars into The City exclusively. Plus, this requires anyone who wants to run around in The City as a woman to create a second avatar as a man if they want to go into MyCareer's story mode. So as awesome as this all is to see, it also feels like a frustrating half-step forward.

New landmarks in The City, Casual Corner and Crew HQ, build out the virtual world to be much more inviting and social. In Casual Corner, beginner-friendly pick-up games, including some that are co-op PvE against rather lowly bots, are happening whenever you want to queue for them. Meanwhile, NBA 2K's clan-like "Crews" system gets a big upgrade in Crew HQ, a space for you and your crew to meet up, practice, play crew-only games, and socialize. 

These two additions will better onboard new players and, by being tied to the Learn 2K suite added in recent years, speak to the team's commitment to not feel so dizzying to new players. They also become two more diverse ways to play in a hub world already full of so many different offerings, from ultra-sweaty Proving Grounds games that ditch the shot meter to The Rec's full-length 5v5 games. 

There's always The Park too, where some players spend the entire year building out their in-game legend and dominating on a particular court as though they actually live in the neighborhood. In more than one corner of the game's social world, these various modes feel big enough to allow you to commit to any of them exclusively and still find a lot to love.

My favorite of The City's modes, Street Kings, is akin to Mortal Kombat's Towers: PvE games against boss-type ballers that escalate in challenge with every match, and where a hype man and an energetic crowd of NPCs cheer you on like a classic And 1 game. Since it first appeared in the series two years ago, it's become my favorite way to play multiplayer in NBA 2K because it allows me and my brother to make lots of progress in The City's various progress bars, like player and season XP, without bumping into players who disrupt the more casual vibe we're aiming for.

Of course, every year I'm compelled to shine a spotlight once more on the over-monetized aspects of The City. Visual Concepts is extremely adept at partnering with authentic-feeling brands that create aspirational cosmetics to purchase and unlock in The City, and that's fine with me, even in its abundance. Personally, I loved getting to walk around in a Portland Fire jersey for the first time, as my home city recently rejoined the WNBA. 

But I will forever hate that players can spend money to improve their players right away. Paying past the grind that begins with players rated 60 overall (OVR) has long been an additional surcharge on players in the game's marquee mode. 

It's also true that avatar intricacies like skill badges, takeover abilities, and cap breakers all mean that initial pay-to-win buff is less effective than it may sound. Paying to bring my 60 OVR player to 79 OVR as soon as he steps into The City isn't as big a leap as grinding him to 99 OVR with multiple cap breakers and gold badges.

Still, it essentially means NBA 2K is not a $70 game, but closer to a $100 game for anyone planning to play online with their friends. Attributes shouldn't be available with the same universal currency that also buys me my Rose City hat and a pair of virtual Jordans. I'll say it every year, even as it seems this is very much a feature for parent company Take-Two, not a bug.

This year's game accidentally shines a light on a related topic, too. With The City taking on the same look (albeit with some added landmarks) as last year's, it serves as a more overt reminder that your purchases don't carry over, even if the virtual world's layout does. I really liked my avatar's Celtics hoodie last year, but seeing it in the shop again for a price, rather than just being available to me for free, felt especially annoying this year. The scenery is nearly identical, but the hoodie was apparently just a rental. There's so much for sale and new things are added frequently; it feels like it's time for NBA 2K to go the way of Fortnite and just let me keep my in-game purchases forever.

The City is normally the social aspect of the custom avatar you'll build in the game, with MyCareer being the solo portion, but this year's game has built co-op into the MyCareer experience. However, it's a half-measure for now, and not as exciting as I once hoped when it was revealed. The narrative of MyCareer is much longer than usual this year, and the co-op portion of play only becomes available after several hours. At that time, the G League team you've landed with in the game's branching saga introduces a new teammate of yours in Trace Miller, a fake player invented for the story and meant to be the Player 2 of the story mode. 

This leaves your co-op friend feeling side-saddled. You can create your own avatar with your own intricately designed player build, even using your own face, but Miller is who he is, for the most part. Though you can choose his starting size and position, the build design tools are much simpler from there. The best version of co-op MyCareer would let both players fully customize their athletes, rather than leaving one feeling like merely the sidekick unlocked after many hours, as this first iteration does. 

The good thing is NBA 2K has long been great at taking an idea and building on it over time, rather than scrapping it if the first year or two don't satisfy players. It's an attribute that has separated this series from some other sports games, and I expect that North Star may affect this mode soon, hopefully for the better.

There's a third way to live out the life of your avatar this year: MyCareer Eras. Borrowing the same remarkably deep Eras feature from the team-based MyNBA mode, MyCareer Eras lets you drop your fake player into any decade from the 1980s Bird vs. Magic era onward, thereby time-traveling to the NBA of yesteryear. In any era, you'll see period-specific presentation elements, rules, uniforms, rosters, and even audience attire.

Eras were introduced in NBA 2K a few years ago, and they remain the coolest way to play Franchise-style. Though you could drop your avatar into MyNBA Eras last year, that was the extent of it. You were just a player on a team like any other. This year's version is a bespoke narrative experience that puts the spotlight on your player in a bygone era, full of challenges and emergent stories. 

Taking my avatar to the early 1990s and seeking to paint over the Jordan dynasty is an incredibly fun thing to do, and just like The City--or MyNBA, which, admittedly, takes a backseat in terms of sweeping changes of its own this year--MyCareer Eras is a mode I could enjoy for hundreds of hours.

Though MyNBA doesn't get much of a look this year, it at least has received major overhauls in recent years. That's more than I can say for the game's suite of WNBA modes. Over the past three seasons and 2K sequels, my emotional investment in the WNBA has grown a lot, and with a local team making its grand reopening this year, I've been so excited to play as them in 2K. But having grown more attached to the league has led me to see some of 2K's shortcomings when it comes to the WNBA.

For one, The W, its solo avatar analog to MyCareer, doesn't allow you to import your woman avatar from The City, which, like the lack of a truly customizable Player 2 in MyCareer, feels like a half-measure. But in MyWNBA mode, where you take on seasons of a single team, there's a lack of the same care the men's league gets.

I'm sure the WNBA modes are played less, but I've always found it commendable how NBA 2K is a hub for all things basketball; only now I'm better able to see some of what's missing, like a robust halftime show and arena-specific ceremonies, the likes of which do exist in the real WNBA but only exist in the 2K version of the NBA.

I'm hopeful that, as the league continues to grow, 2K's WNBA modes can grow with it. It's great to see women in the game more, like in The City or in MyTeam, where they first arrived last year, but in their own bespoke game modes, some of the details this studio is otherwise so great at building into the experience are lacking.

I've spent a lot of words on not talking about gameplay, which might seem weird, but it's because this year's game feels the most year-over-year familiar to me of any game of recent memory. That's not exactly a bad thing. NBA 2K is a lot of fun on the court. It has been, so it is again. And it's not that the game adds nothing. In particular, I really like the new step-through finishing moves, used to finish a shot after you've lost your dribble. Like other aspects of on-court animations, lots of these are modeled after real players' go-to moves.

Visual Concepts has been using ProPlay, its in-house tech that transposes real NBA footage into gameplay animations, in ways that are hard to specifically attribute from outside the confines of the studio, but if ProPlay is why the game looks and feels so good, I'll take it. Combined with the game's continuing efforts to teach newcomers how to play 2K, as well as changes in The City, it feels like the series has never been more approachable.

While playing online can bring out any number of cheesy players who seek to break the game in their favor, this is true of all sports games and is usually improved upon if you stick to specific modes, like Rec games, where the crowded court of 5v5 gameplay minimizes any cheesehead's worst intentions. In games against the computer, I continue to be amazed by how different players and teams--even those spanning different eras--have their own playstyles. 

Playing the Celtics, you'll get a heavy dose of Mazzulla Ball, while the Spurs rightly center everything around the unique size and talents of Wemby. This is a fun basketball game not just because of the depth and breadth of its modes, but also because its foundational gameplay is easy to enjoy and closely resembles watching the real thing.

Overall though, if NBA 2K is truly competing against itself, this year's game is a slight step back. While the addition of co-op to MyCareer and women to The City are great first drafts of ideas, they each come with caveats for now that keep them from being as fun as they could've been--and reasonably should've been. On the court itself, NBA 2K is still a lot of fun, but it has seemingly settled into a groove for now, iterating in smaller ways after previous years' bigger leaps. There's room to grow in the WNBA side of the game, though with The City, MyCareer, and Eras modes, it's not short on deeply immersive experiences already. 

I have enough fun with NBA 2K each year that I tend to delete it from my console after the new year; otherwise, I risk never playing anything else. It can be that good. But just as I was ready to commit to the game for the full year, with my heightened fandom in tow, it's given me an installment I feel more comfortable walking away from--right after I delete the Jordan dynasty and beat all the Street Kings.

event_model_payload.headline: Who Should Receive Farkas’ Ring In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – The Ring Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you having doubts as to who should receive Farkas' Ring in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Farkas, the jester for Mad Khan Bakir, has a deal for you. Of course, it's up to you if you want to push through with the idea or if you feel like you should renege on it. But if you change your mind, you'll have to find someone who'll take the item.

In This Article
  • The Ring quest - Should Farkas or someone else get the ring?

    • Who else can take the ring?
      • Anca
      • Bakr-Erga, the Uriash Matriarch
      • Sanzhani Tsarina

The Ring quest - Should Farkas or someone else get the ring?

The Ring in The Blood of Dawnwalker is actually a follow-up mission. Your main objective is to defeat the Mad Khan, Bakir, as part of the Lunar Game quest. Here’s a brief rundown:

  • Once you’ve angered Bakir, his jester, Farkas, will approach you and hatch a plan. This leads to the Lunar Game quest where you have to become the sole survivor of a deadly maze.
  • Farkas just wants you to bring him an item, a ring with an amethyst that’s supposed to be a family heirloom.
  • If you can enter Bakir’s treasure room and beat him there, you’ll find said item--also known as the Ring with the Purple Eye--on one of the shelves.

What happens if you give the ring to Farkas?

At first glance, you might just want to hand over the ring to Farkas in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you talk to him, he’ll say that Bakir gravely abused his younger brother, and the ring might be the only thing that could reverse his condition. That seems like a noble cause.

There’s just one problem: The ring has demonic runes inscribed on it, and Farkas has absolutely no clue about arcane rituals. Giving it to him is going to be a huge risk. Still, if you decide to do it, just know that things won’t bode well for Farkas and his brother, as you’ll find out much later at the end of the game.

Who else can take the ring?

Of course, you can also choose not to give the item to Farkas. This will kickstart The Ring quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Your goal is to find someone who knows more about the ring, which means looking for people who dabble in magic and sorcery.

Note: As of the time of this writing, we know of three NPCs that can receive the item. Note that giving the ring to them does cost 2x Time Segments.

Anca

You can give the ring to Anca at the Crossroads Inn. She’ll destroy it and hand you the Quick Fighter’s Ring as a replacement. It’s an epic accessory that has maximum human health, human health restoration, and swordmastery ability cooldown.

Bakr-Erga, the Uriash Matriarch

Alternatively, you can give the item to the Uriash Matriarch, provided that you’ve already discovered the Hidden Uriash Village as part of the Song of the Mountain quest. You’ll receive the Vrakhir’s Endurance, an epic amulet that has physical damage reduction, magical damage reduction, and blood drinking restoration.

Sanzhani Tsarina

Lastly, you can hand over the accessory to the Sanzhani Tsarina, assuming you’ve already done the Good Home/Letters to Lunka questline. Surprisingly enough, the Tsarina still gives you the Vrakhir’s Endurance amulet, similar to what you’d get from the Uriash Matriarch.

The Uriash Matriarch (left) and Sanzhani Tsarina (right) give you the same reward.

That does it for our guide on how to complete The Ring in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Since we’re talking about strange magics and sorceries, you might want to read about the Home Sweet Home time loop.

event_model_payload.headline: How To Complete The Gilded Gauntlet In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – Ambrus Boss Guide
event_model_payload.summary:
Are you planning to complete The Gilded Gauntlet in The Blood of Dawnwalker? This quest is the culmination of your efforts to stymy Ambrus, the arrogant vampire boyar who’s also one of Brencis’ lieutenants. Our guide has all the details that you need, but be ready for a few spoilers. We tackle not just The Gilded Gauntlet, but also a related mission called The Bittersweet Toast.

In This Article
  • Ambrus’ end - The Gilded Gauntlet and The Bittersweet Toast
    • The Bittersweet Toast: Time progression
    • The Bittersweet Toast: The ritual for Iulian
    • The Gilded Gauntlet: Drinking with Ambrus
    • The Gilded Gauntlet: Ambrus boss fight
    • The Gilded Gauntlet: Ambrus’ death and rewards

Ambrus’ end - The Gilded Gauntlet and The Bittersweet Toast

The Gilded Gauntlet quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker becomes available after you’ve fully angered Ambrus. That means you just need to keep sabotaging his blood transports, leech collectors, and other operations until the quest pops up in your journal. Once it’s available, track it and go to the town of Maragir. As soon as you approach the area with crucified people, a cutscene will play.

The Bittersweet Toast: Time progression

The mere act of approaching the yard already costs 1x Time Segment. From there, should you wish to battle Ambrus immediately, you have to ring the bell at the ruins to start your duel. This can only be done at night and it costs 2x Time Segments.

However, if you want to make the fight a lot easier, you can undertake a side quest called The Bittersweet Toast. That’s where a nobleman, Iulian, hatches a plan that will surely weaken Ambrus. Consider this option carefully since it uses up a lot of Time Segments.

Follow Iulian's servant (left) to learn about a sneaky plan (right).

The Bittersweet Toast: The ritual for Iulian

The Bittersweet Toast quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker has the following steps:

  • Go with Iulian’s servant to his home. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Chat with Iulian and agree to his plan. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Go to Vera’s hut with Iulian. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Inspect the alchemy table in Vera’s hut. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Examine Vera’s remains at the altar and ask Iulian what happens next. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Look for Vera’s ritual scroll. This costs 1x Time Segment.
  • Perform the ritual by using Astral Communion on the altars. You’ll periodically fight spectral enemies, and then you’ll have to force-feed Iulian with the poison. This whole sequence costs 3x Time Segments.

All in all, you’re looking at 9x Time Segments for The Bittersweet Toast. But there are additional caveats:

  • Remember, you can only start your duel with Ambrus at night. The action of ringing the bell to summon Ambrus still requires 2x Time Segments. This means you should only do this a bit earlier in the evening, not when it’s almost daybreak.
  • Vera’s poison is now coursing through Iulian’s veins. That’s why there’s an additional requirement that you have to “show up on time”--i.e. You must duel Ambrus within three days of finishing The Bittersweet Toast.

The Gilded Gauntlet: Drinking with Ambrus

Regardless of how you handled The Bittersweet Toast, you still have to do The Blood of Dawnwalker Gilded Gauntlet quest. Assuming it’s nighttime, go ahead and ring the bell. Once Ambrus and his lackeys arrive, you should see Iulian with them.

Coen and Ambrus will have a chat. Pick any reply you want until Ambrus says that the two of you need to have a toast first. There are four options:

  • “Gladly! To a juicy slaughter!” - Both Coen and Ambrus will feed on Iulian and both will get poisoned. Coen’s status effect only lasts briefly, but Ambrus’ will persist until the end of the battle.
  • “I don’t drink from humans.” - Ambrus will gut Iulian and kill him outright. Iulian’s blood will seep through Ambrus’ skin, causing him to get poisoned. Unfortunately, this debuff only lasts for a single health segment.
  • “Letting a peasant drink first? What kind of a boyar are you?” and “I don’t trust anything you offer.” - Only Ambrus will drink from Iulian. The poison will persist throughout the battle.

The Gilded Gauntlet: Ambrus boss fight

If you never went through with Iulian’s plan, then Ambrus won’t be poisoned at all. You have to fight him normally, so watch out for his lightning-fast melee strikes.

  • He’ll often teleport away, and then charge up a lunging attack or a spinning slice attack.
  • He also deftly defends your blows--i.e. you have to do perfect blocks, followed by ripostes, to land a hit on him.
  • Ambrus' ability, Scarlet Shield, also heals him if you attack him while it's active.
  • Later once he’s down to his last health segment, he’ll continuously teleport and stab at your location.

Conversely, if Iulian’s blood was poisoned and Ambrus fed on him (via the aforementioned dialogue options), then Ambrus boss fight will be significantly easier. You just have to keep dodging whenever he does his unblockable attacks. Eventually, Ambrus will die from the poison.

Note: If you picked “I don’t drink from humans,” the poison effect won’t last as long. You have to fight Ambrus normally for the remainder of his health bar.

The Gilded Gauntlet: Ambrus’ death and rewards

Regardless of how you took down Ambrus, you’ll be given a chance to drink his blood. Here how things will pan out:

  • You’ll be teleported to Anachora, the hellish realm for lost vrakhiri souls. You can invite Ambrus in if you want to spare him an eternity of suffering.
  • The Scarlet Shield ability is automatically unlocked. It restores a portion of your vampiric health after a perfect block, with a chance to trigger from directional blocks and omniblocks.
  • You can loot Ambrus’ Cuirass from his ashes. This legendary heavy chestpiece has vampiric ability cooldown, attack stamina cost, AC restoration (attacks), and AC restoration (blocks).
  • Ambrus’ weapon, the Sword of Valor, is epic-tier. It has damage against mortals, AC restoration (actions), and AC restoration (passive).

As for Iulian, he sadly didn’t survive the ordeal. The poison coursing through his body, coupled with being drained of blood, were just too much to bear. You can bury his body, though, which costs 1x Time Segment.

That does it for our guide on how to complete The Gilded Gauntlet in The Blood of Dawnwalker. You’ve just taken out one of Brencis’ lieutenants. Perhaps you’re planning on eliminating the others. If you’re raring to go, you can head over to our Bakir: The Lunar Game guide and Xanthe: The Cycle of Love guide.

event_model_payload.summary:
As pretty as Cities: Skylines is, getting a read on your city's problems can take some digging. While traffic jams are immediately visible, prompting you to start reorganising the layout of your streets and bypasses, other issues only make themselves known when you switch on overlays or bring up a stats screen. Changing that is one developer Iceflake Studios aims for colourful plastic brick-based spinoff Lego Skylines.

"If there's an issue, it should be visible in the world," game director Lasse Liljedahl tells me. "Everything that you need to worry about or manage is something you should see while zooming in and zooming out and not digging deep in statistics or information screens. That's the goal."

Miami-Dade sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz and commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez have already spoken out against the potential deal, observing in a joint statement that "we should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence.”

event_model_payload.headline: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is best when it's silly, and despite some gloomy open world slogging, sometimes even remembers it
event_model_payload.summary:
The opening minutes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword are glorious, in the sense that they’re utterly shambolic. Wandering ronin Musashi wakes up under a bridge, belts a wrong-footingly British "WOT?!" at some starving urchins eyeing up his rice ball, then proceeds to be chased around a muddy village by what feels like two thousand martial arts students, only occasionally stopping to boot a wooden plank into their faces or scoop up an imperilled dog. It’s goofy and brash and genuinely funny, in a way that immediately looks to elevate it among the field of po-faced fantasy slashers as effectively as any well-honed parry mechanic.

Why in the following hours, then, does Way of the Sword make only occasional attempts to match this intro’s energy?

The campaign was successful and many games were impacted. The campaign's had a chilling effect, leaving developers making games including any sexual content in a kind of limbo as to whether digital storefronts will host their work. Some are ushered through without issue, while others are banned with little recourse.

Just last week, we saw how Valve blocked Molleindustria's Future? No Thanks! due to its scenes of minor nudity. Then, only after public lobbying, did they manage to get Valve to reconsider and rescind their ban.

So, after playing a half hour demo of Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival, a demo set almost entirely inside a fetish club, and one featuring male nudity, female nudity, and some pretty sexually explicit content, I asked the developers if they were worried about a Steam ban or if it had led to any changes to the game.
